item.title: Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
item.description: Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.

item.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
item.description: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

item.title: Fruitcake weather! Truman Capote reads 'A Christmas Memory'
item.description: Truman Capote's Christmas short story tells of 7-year-old Buddy and his elderly cousin Sook as they celebrate the holidays. Together they gather ingredients to bake fruitcakes, and cut down a Christmas tree. With illustrations from NPR's Jackie Lay.

item.title: Buying new things feels wonderful. But it can also be a trap
item.description: Constantly buying new things can be problematic, says journalist Eric Athas, author of the new book "Saying No to New." Here's how to break the cycle and find joy in what you already have.
